proposals.before: Lou Jing said: 'Your Majesty took all-under-heaven differs from Zhou house.
proposals.after: Lou Jing said: 'Your Majesty took all-under-heaven differently from the Zhou house.
proposals.reason: Literal English is ungrammatical ("differs" without a subject auxiliary); the Chinese contrasts how the empire was obtained.

proposals.before: He was defeated at Dingtao and followed the Huai King.
proposals.after: After the defeat at Dingtao, he followed the Huai King.
proposals.reason: The silent subject who follows King Huai is Shusun Tong; Xiang Liang was the one defeated at Dingtao, so "he was defeated" misattributes the defeat.

proposals.before: When Shusun Tong went out, he gave each of the scholars five hundred jin of gold.
proposals.after: When Shusun Tong went out, he gave the five hundred jin of gold to the scholars.
proposals.reason: Chinese 皆以五百斤金賜諸生 refers to distributing the previously bestowed five hundred jin, not five hundred jin to each scholar; the idiomatic rendering matches the narrative.

proposals.before: He then went, arrived at Pingcheng, and the Xiongnu indeed sent crack troops that surrounded the Gao Emperor at Baiteng. Only after seven days did he get release.
proposals.after: He then went, arrived at Pingcheng, and the Xiongnu indeed sent crack troops that surrounded the Gao Emperor at Baideng. Only after seven days did he get release.
proposals.reason: 白登 is Baideng; "Baiteng" is a corrupted romanization inconsistent with the idiomatic line.

decisions.reason: Focus Chinese 取天下與周室異 contrasts how the empire was obtained with the Zhou house. The original literal "took all-under-heaven differs" is ungrammatical; "differently from the Zhou house" restores that contrast without changing speaker or sense.

Preceding unit has Shusun Tong follow Xiang Liang; 敗於定陶，從懷王 then marks the Dingtao defeat as circumstance before he follows King Huai. "He was defeated" wrongly makes Shusun the defeated party; "After the defeat at Dingtao, he followed the Huai King" keeps the biography's subject as follower only.

皆以五百斤金賜諸生 means he used that five-hundred-jin sum to reward the scholars, not that each received five hundred jin. Removing "each of" corrects the quantity error while matching the narrative and idiomatic sense.
白登 is Baideng; "Baiteng" is a wrong romanization of the same place name. The proposed literal only corrects that reading and leaves the siege narrative intact.
